findings.title: Public optimizer clipping consumes scaled gradients with fused AMP SGD.
findings.trigger: MixedPrecisionStepStrategy composed with GradientClippingOptimizerStrategy(DefaultOptimizerStrategy), registry SGD fused=True, real CPU torch.amp.GradScaler. Scalar parameter 1, quadratic loss w^2, lr .1, max_norm 1, initial scale 8.
findings.cause_and_impact: The step prehook clips gradient 16 to about 1. AMP-aware fused SGD then unscales it by 8 inside the optimizer. A finite, completed training update is substantially too small. Nonfused GradScaler unscales before optimizer.step and passes the same numerical reference.

reproducer.selection: Commands run the complete five-case independent negative suite; the named node identifies this failure. No assertions skipped or weakened.

findings.root_default_scale_corrob: Actual ComposableTrainer, loss 10*w and scale 65536 gives 0.9999984502792358 instead of 0.900000009999999 on both versions. Root source/raw receipts independently hash-checked; reviewer separately constructed scale-8 reference.
findings.test_gap: Existing actual fused/nonfused overflow tests exercise skip counting but do not combine a finite AMP update with the public clipping wrapper.
findings.bounded_acceptance: Clipping must consume unscaled gradients for actual fused and nonfused AMP. Preserve real overflow skip/update counting and accumulation-tail behavior; numerical parameter-reference regression required.
findings.limits: Actual CPU fused/nonfused Torch execution. CPU injection leaves CUDA autocast disabled with the recorded warning; no CUDA execution claim.

findings.title: Long logical names produce worker files that pause_training does not remove.
findings.trigger: Actual train_process and test_process with max_concurrency=1, model_name="x"*240, client 7 and the actual run PID, followed by pause_training.
findings.expected: Remove this worker/client/run model, history and evaluation artifacts, retaining unrelated owners and persistent files.
findings.actual_each_python: Accuracy file is removed, but three owned files remain: ~t<tuple_digest>.safetensors, its .pkl history and ~t<tuple_digest>.eval.pkl.
findings.cause_and_impact: pause_training encodes a suffixless name and later appends extensions. The writer encodes the complete name with its suffix; suffix length and the 251-byte primary/history limit can change whether the tuple is digested. Cleanup silently leaves potentially large temporary model files and private worker state.

reproducer.selection: Commands run the complete five-case independent negative suite; the named node identifies this failure. No assertions skipped or weakened.

findings.test_gap: The long-name default save/load regression verifies successful file creation but does not call actual worker writers and cleanup. Short ordinary/slash-name cleanup passes.
findings.bounded_acceptance: Derive each cleanup artifact through the same complete logical-name/suffix contract as its writer; model history follows its actual primary filename. Verify long, ordinary and special names and unrelated-owner preservation. Preserve accepted B F10 cleanup ownership.

findings.expected: Read the same-client accepted B vector, preserve the original, prefer canonical state if present, and never adopt client 0.

reproducer.selection: Commands run the complete five-case independent negative suite; the named node identifies this failure. No assertions skipped or weakened.

test_gap.detail: Test handcrafts root + "feddyn_grad_1.pth", copying the new reader spelling rather than using accepted B writer output.

findings.title: FedALA loses returning logical-client state when disk persistence is disabled.
findings.trigger: FedALAUpdateStrategy(save_state=False), physical trainer client 1 -> 2 -> 1, with client 1 trained before reassignment. The documented flag controls persistence to disk, not logical in-memory ownership.
findings.expected: Returning client 1 continues its own local model, learned ALA weights and start_phase. Given identical incoming model and data, its update matches a dedicated client-1 trainer.
findings.cause_and_impact: Identity change clears local_model_state, weights and start_phase with no per-client memory cache; _load_state restores only when save_state=True. Returning client therefore takes first-round initialization, bypasses adaptive aggregation, and changes the next-round weights by up to 1.1351019144058228.

reproducer.selection: Commands run the complete five-case independent negative suite; the named node identifies this failure. No assertions skipped or weakened.

findings.test_gap: Existing save_state=False worker coverage keeps the same client. Existing 1->2->1 FedALA ownership coverage uses default disk persistence, which hides the missing in-memory cache.
findings.bounded_acceptance: Keep and restore per-owner in-memory FedALA state when disk persistence is disabled, preserving cross-client isolation and successful worker returns. Dedicated-vs-reassigned numerical continuation must agree.
